question: Brihadiswara Temple which exhibits Dravidian temple architecture is located in __________.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Thanjavur**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Brihadiswara Temple** is located in **Thanjavur**, Tamil Nadu.
 
• It is one of the largest South Indian temples and an exemplary example of **Dravidian architecture**.
 
• The temple was built by **Raja Raja Chola I** in 1010 AD.
 
• It is a part of the **UNESCO World Heritage Site** known as the "Great Living Chola Temples".
 
• The temple is dedicated to **Lord Shiva** and is also known as **Peruvudaiyar Kovil**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The temple's **Vimana (temple tower)** is one of the tallest of its kind in the world.
 
• The temple is renowned for its **architectural brilliance** and intricate **sculptures**.
 
• The temple complex includes a massive **statue of Nandi (sacred bull)**, carved out of a single stone.
 
• It is an important pilgrimage site and a major tourist attraction in Tamil Nadu.
 
• The Brihadiswara Temple stands as a testament to the **Chola dynasty's** contribution to art, architecture, and culture.
